Not RTC before warmup; no measured spike data. Both browsers and service cleaned up. Same frozen inputs subsequently passed spike-A and spike-B in c2.

interpretation.baselineAnomaly: c2/A2 passed correctness at about 15.27 logical Hz with P0/P1 resimulation 33/4875. Kept without exclusion. Repeat baseline c3/A1 was about 39.33 Hz, c3/A2 about 49.30 Hz. Cause not isolated.
interpretation.candidateObservation: Four stable-delay candidate sessions stayed around 48.2-48.8 logical Hz; this does not isolate a causal wall-time gain.
boundaries: Two headed Chrome processes on native Intel GPU; CPU rate 4 on both pages is not a phone model.
79 +/- 5 ms is application-send delay, including repair, not measured wire RTT. Signaling relay is local.
120 Hz is the Page touch schedule target. Actual down/move submissions are coalesced; tapes differ and are not captured per-frame input tapes.
Callback duration is wall time after callback entry, excluding rAF dispatch wait and observer tail; not CPU self time.
Present and frontier gaps are observer metrics; first changed event anchors are excluded.
LogicalFps measures simulation-frontier advancement, not display FPS. Network-driven pacing below 60 Hz alone does not establish dropped display frames or CPU cost.
Timing rows end at frame 1200; final confirmation/reconcile tail is outside the body metrics.
Recovery windows start at injection-window end. Last delayed sends can arrive later; 1-second window classifications are not precise network-drain or latency timestamps.
Browser flags request disabling background throttling, but no OS focus/visibility/occlusion trace was collected.
No phone, remote relay/public-network, full managed Launcher, audio-output, dense-stage or all-scene acceptance.
